title: Larry Robbins pitches at Sohn Investment Conference 2026
description: Larry Robbins, CEO, Glenview Capital pitches several stocks for Sohn 2026, including Global Payments, Genius Sports, AMD, CVS, Teva, Viatris, Tenet Healthcare and more.
summary: The speaker argues that several healthcare and financial services companies are undervalued relative to their growth potential and operational improvements. Specifically, the pitch highlights attractive valuations for Global Payments, Genius Sports, and CVS, while also expressing a constructive view on pharmaceuticals like Teva and Viatris due to their free cash flow and pipeline value. Additionally, the speaker identifies Tenet Healthcare as a successful turnaround story with strong management and active buybacks driving potential stock performance.

claims.claim: The speaker is bullish on Global Payments, citing execution, share gains, buybacks, and a valuation of four times earnings.
claims.quote: Starting with Global Payments, which I pitched last year and I will pitch it again this year because in fact they hit every number. Yes, they do process transactions for Middle East Airlines that are obviously going through a very, very unique travel disruption that took literally 0.2% out of volume growth last quarter and may take 1% of volume growth out of the year, but the company continues to execute. Their leverage will be down to three times. Their genius product is in fact genius taking share in the marketplace. We have Elliott on the board. We have Silver Lake on the board and they will buy back 7 and 1/2 billion dollars worth of stock. You get uh what we believe is accelerating earnings growth that will be above 20%. What are you paying for that? Four, yes, four times earnings.
claims.speaker: Larry Robbins

claims.claim: The speaker views Genius Sports as a great business with long-term contracts, price escalators, and a low valuation despite recent acquisitions.
claims.quote: Um we're involved with a small company called Genius Sports uh ticker g e n i. They are the data layer that sits between the NFL and your sports gambling so that we can verify whether in fact uh how much yardage that happened, what was the play per percentage or all those prop bets as well as the bets on the overall games. Uh their contracts within the gaming side, 75% of revenues are long-term contractual. They have 20% price escalators. This is as good of a business as we have seen. They did an acquisition in February at the time that private credit markets were collapsing. People did not like acquisitions. They did not like levering. We like the acquisition. We have them trading at four times our 28 earnings estimate uh for a company that we believe it's going to grow top line 20, EBITDA and EBIT 30 trading at four times they are levered today. We believe that their leverage will be under one times inclusive of paying an earnout on success of that acquisition.
claims.speaker: Larry Robbins

claims.claim: The speaker believes CVS is attractive after cultural changes and CEO replacement, with earnings potentially doubling and a valuation of 10 times earnings.
claims.quote: Which brings me to then my beloved CVS of which I'm still on the board. The company has made an enormous amount of progress in the last 18 months since I and three others joined the board since they changed their CEO, since they changed their culture and that they begun the process of repairing they're all the way up to 10 times earnings, which is again, looks to be extremely attractive to us. Now, all this is public available information. There's nothing that's proprietary. This was Glenview's slide that we shared with the top 450 managers 1 year ago, in April of 2025, to explain to them what we think that the implied earnings trajectory would be if we simply went in the Aetna businesses, as well as a business called Oak Street that they were losing money. If they went from losing to break even, and then break even to target margins over a period of years, here's the earnings that it would unlock. And in fact, we thought that the earnings could double on that alone. That means no generation of cash flow. That means no growth in either businesses. Just literally that could double earnings. And we would point out that of that earnings growth that is that was there as potential, 2/3 of that simply came from fixing the Medicare Advantage business. The company is well on its way towards repairing the company. They've had five straight quarters of beating raises. Leverage of the company has come down significantly from just under five times to 4.1 Moody's adjusted, 3.5 on a straight-up basis. They've gone from $0 in Aetna to $4 of Aetna. They still have much more to go. There's a very exciting tech initiative they have called Health 100 that will reveal itself over the course of the next 12 months. And that they will finally be in a position to deploy offensive capital at year end or in the beginning of next year as their leverage will come back and support their strong investment grade credit ratings.
claims.speaker: Larry Robbins

claims.claim: The speaker remains constructive on Teva despite progress, citing increased pipeline value and a valuation of 11 times earnings for 20% earnings growth.
claims.quote: We continue to like Teva despite its progress. The pipeline last year we said was worth three to $9 a share. The TL1A product continues to get great data. We believe the pipeline value has increased to six to $12 a share. The company is one year closer to the margin goals of hitting 30% margin target. We believe that you're going to see 20% earnings growth next year in order to get from point A in 26 to point B. The company's trading at 11 and change times next year's earnings for that type of earnings growth and pointing out that if you value the pipeline and back out the stick value cuz the pipeline does not contribute to earnings until 2029 or 2030, that you're paying seven and a half times for the core business with a management team that clearly has to be viewed as having tremendous credibility.
claims.speaker: Larry Robbins

claims.claim: The speaker is constructive on Viatris (Teva Light) due to its high free cash flow yield and optionality, despite different pipeline risks.
claims.quote: Um if you think you missed Teva, Teva light is called Viatris. That stock also has doubled. It's all the way up to six times earnings, which means yes, it was trading at three times earnings a year and a half ago. Their pipeline is different. It's not quite as a major blockbuster. It has a little bit more risk towards it, but we are constructive about their pipeline. We are constructive about the overall balance sheet and capital employment. It's trading with a very very high free cash flow yield and we think there's lots of good optionality to that.
claims.speaker: Larry Robbins

claims.claim: The speaker views Tenet Healthcare as a successful turnaround with strong management, active buybacks, and potential for significant stock performance.
claims.quote: And then finally, I would mention the fact that when we say together we build, we mean it. We revamped the board of Tenet Healthcare almost a decade ago. It's been one of the best turnarounds that we've seen in healthcare. They continue to provide more for less. Their ASCs continue to grow, which provide healthcare and surgeries at a lower cost setting than an acute hospital. I would look at the stock price chart on the top right and note that while the stock has tripled, that's because the earnings tripled. We've had absolutely no multiple expansion despite the fact that the leverage has come way down, the portfolio has evolved, and Dr. Sam Sataria, as CEO, has proven himself to be, honestly, one of the top CEOs that we've ever seen throughout our 25 years. The company has an active buyback plan. If they were to fix leverage at three times EBITDA, they could buy back two-thirds of the company at these at these prices over the next few years. We don't think that's going to happen because we think the stock will continue to perform quite well.
claims.speaker: Larry Robbins
